verdict.reason: This is a coherent public API rename: Val becomes the canonical literal-value spec and Literal remains an alias, with internal evaluation updated to recognize Val. Existing users retain compatibility while new usage and reprs use Val.
verdict.unchecked_changes: Documentation and docstring updates, including the compatibility note and references across API examples, are not directly exercised by the fail-to-pass tests.
verdict.title: Make Val the canonical literal-value spec while preserving Literal compatibility
verdict.statement: The spec wrapper for returning a value literally is currently exposed as `Literal`, while `Val` is also present but does not work consistently in all contexts. In particular, `Val(T)` used as a dynamic path component in `S` expressions is treated as a mapping key rather than evaluated, so specs that need to refer to a literal value such as `T` fail with a path access error. Make `Val` the canonical wrapper that evaluates to its wrapped value, including when used as a path component, and keep `Literal` as a backwards-compatible alias to `Val`. The alias and canonical name should refer to the same class; its repr should use `Val(...)`.
